newsitem.title: CANADA: Drivers to eat and surf at roadside truckstop kiosks.
newsitem.headline: Drivers to eat and surf at roadside truckstop kiosks.

text.p: U.S. Truckers will soon be able to check their e-mail and browse for new jobs when they stop to refuel at truck stops under a new system announced on Monday called Driver Net.

King Products Inc of Mississauga, Ontario, said it was awarded a US$3.3 million contract to provide hardware and software for the new kiosk-based system being produced by TIMM Communications Inc of Joplin, Missouri.
King said it hoped to deliver some 400 flat-panel, multimedia kiosks for the system over the next year, beginning in February.
The kiosks with CD-quality sound will allow drivers to retrieve information on truck stop promotions, employment opportunities with trucking firms and information on points of interest.
Each kiosk will be equipped with a printer, telephone handset, smart card and credit card reader, stereo speakers, and will be powered by an Intel Corp Pentium chip.
A King spokesman said initially the communications and the e-mail network will be delivered via a telephone-based communications system without access to the Internet.
